config.title: Styled Component Pattern

intro.title: Styled Component Pattern
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile card using the Styled Component pattern to style your React components. You will learn how to write CSS directly within your JavaScript files using the styled-components library, creating reusable and scoped styles. The main technologies involved are React, JavaScript (JSX), and the styled-components package. This approach helps keep your styles modular and tied to specific components, making your code easier to maintain and understand.
intro.usecase: The Styled Component pattern is widely used in modern React applications to create reusable, self-contained UI components with encapsulated styles. You'll see this pattern in design systems for consistent buttons, form inputs, and navigation menus across entire applications. Product teams use it for building interactive dashboards with themed panels, modals, and data visualization widgets that maintain consistent styling. This approach is particularly valuable when creating complex UI libraries or maintaining large-scale applications where visual consistency and component isolation are critical.

objectives: Implement a styled component using the styled-components library
Apply dynamic styling to a component based on props
Construct a theme provider to manage global styles
Configure nested styling within a styled component
Update component styles using the css helper function
Integrate styled components with existing React components
Manipulate component variants using conditional styling

steps.title: Import React and styled-components
steps.instruction: Import React and the styled function from styled-components.
steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of your file. You'll need two imports: one for React and one for styled.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and styled from styled-components here
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary imports to use React and styled-components.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react' and styled is imported from 'styled-components'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and the styled function from styled-components.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statements. You need to import React from 'react' and styled from 'styled-components'.

steps.title: Create a basic styled component
steps.instruction: Create a styled component named 'StyledBox' using the styled function from styled-components. Make it a div with some basic CSS styling like a background color and padding.
steps.hint: Use the styled function to create a styled div component. For example: styled.div`css rules`
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a StyledBox component that can be used like a regular React component but with built-in CSS styling.
successCriteria: A styled component named StyledBox is created using styled.div with CSS properties like background-color and padding
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a styled component named StyledBox with some CSS styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a styled component using the styled function from styled-components.

steps.title: Use the styled component in JSX
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named StyledComponentDemo that returns your styled component in JSX.
steps.hint: Define a component that renders your styled component like any other React element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component that renders your styled component will be created.
successCriteria: The StyledComponentDemo component is defined and returns your styled component in JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your component returns the styled component you created earlier.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined a component named StyledComponentDemo that returns your styled component.

steps.title: Add props to styled components
steps.instruction: Modify your existing styled component to accept a 'color' prop and use it to set the text color dynamically.
steps.hint: In styled-components, you can access props inside template literals using ${props => props.propName}. For example: color: ${props => props.color || 'black'};
steps.expectedOutcome: The styled component should now accept a 'color' prop and use it to set the text color.
successCriteria: The styled component uses template literal interpolation with props to set the color CSS property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to use the 'color' prop inside the template literal to set the text color.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Remember to modify the styled component to accept a 'color' prop and use it in the CSS.

steps.title: Create multiple styled components
steps.instruction: Create a second styled component named 'StyledButton' that renders a button element with some basic styling.
steps.hint: Use the same styled function syntax you used for the first component, but this time create a button element with properties like background color, padding, and border radius.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have two styled components defined: one from earlier steps and a new StyledButton component with button styling.
successCriteria: A styled component named StyledButton is created using styled.button with at least three CSS properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a styled component, but make sure it's named exactly 'StyledButton' and uses styled.button with at least three CSS properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Remember to use styled.button and define CSS properties inside template literals.

steps.title: Style existing React components
steps.instruction: Create a new functional React component named 'CustomButton' that returns a simple button element with the text 'Click me'.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns a <button>Click me</button> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a basic React component ready to be styled with styled-components in the next step.
successCriteria: A functional component named CustomButton is defined and returns a button element with the text 'Click me'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component is named exactly 'CustomButton' and returns a button element with the text 'Click me'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a functional component named CustomButton that returns <button>Click me</button>.

steps.title: Add hover effects with styled-components
steps.instruction: Add a hover effect to your CustomButton styled component using &:hover to change its background color when hovered.
steps.hint: Inside the styled.button template literal, add &:hover { background-color: #0056b3; } after the existing styles.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CustomButton component will have a hover effect that changes its background color to a darker blue when the mouse hovers over it.
successCriteria: CustomButton includes &:hover with a background-color property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added &:hover with a background-color change inside the styled.button template literal.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hover effect wasn't added correctly. Check that you've used &:hover inside the styled.button template literal with a background-color property.

steps.title: Import ThemeProvider and create a theme object
steps.instruction: Import ThemeProvider from 'styled-components' and create a theme object with a primary color property.
steps.hint: Import ThemeProvider alongside styled, then define a theme object with a key like 'primaryColor' and a hex color value.
steps.expectedOutcome: ThemeProvider is imported and a theme object is defined with at least one property.
successCriteria: ThemeProvider is imported from 'styled-components' and a theme object is created with a property like primaryColor.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've imported ThemeProvider from 'styled-components' and created a theme object with at least one property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement and theme object creation. You need to import ThemeProvider and define a theme object with properties.

steps.title: Wrap app with ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: In your StyledComponentDemo component, wrap the existing content with the ThemeProvider component and pass the theme object as a prop.
steps.hint: Import ThemeProvider from 'styled-components' if not already imported, then wrap your JSX content with <ThemeProvider theme={theme}>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider wraps the component tree, making the theme available to all styled components.
successCriteria: The StyledComponentDemo component returns JSX wrapped in ThemeProvider with a theme prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've wrapped the content with ThemeProvider and passed the theme object as a prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check if you've imported ThemeProvider, created a theme object, and wrapped your JSX content with <ThemeProvider theme={theme}>.

steps.title: Access theme in styled components
steps.instruction: Modify the StyledDiv component to use a background color from the theme object instead of the hardcoded 'lightblue'.
steps.hint: Use the theme prop inside the styled component's template literal, like: ${props => props.theme.colors.primary}
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledDiv component will now use a theme value for its background color, making it theme-aware.
successCriteria: StyledDiv component uses props.theme to access a color value instead of hardcoded 'lightblue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're accessing the theme through props.theme and using it in the background-color property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StyledDiv component still uses hardcoded 'lightblue'. Try using ${props => props.theme.colors.primary} or similar theme property.
